summary.prose: Building this Story adds a self-contained team-policy module (policy file parser, per-repository sighting record and lock, anchor finder, reader, refresh and starter writer) and two command-bar commands, team init and team refresh, that expose it. The work is ordered so each piece is tested against real git before the next builds on it, and the existing gate code is not touched.

tasks.title: Team types, PATHS entry and policy-file parser
tasks.summary: Add the ~/.insrc/team directory entry to PATHS in src/shared/paths.ts, and create src/workflow/team/ with the types (TeamPolicy including source.anchorKnown, PolicyResult, PolicyAnchor, PolicyRefreshOutcome) and the parser that validates .insrc/policy.json against the authored-fields schema (teamMode, signoffStages, claimsEnforced, administrators), rejecting unknown fields, wrong types, and files carrying claimUnits, forceTaskIssues or source, and that derives claimUnits and forceTaskIssues itself.
acceptanceChecks: A valid policy file parses to a TeamPolicy with the fixed claimUnits and forceTaskIssues true.
Bad JSON, an unknown field, a wrong type, or a file carrying claimUnits, forceTaskIssues or source is rejected with a reason.
PATHS exposes the team directory used by the sighting store.

tasks.title: Sighting store and per-repository lock
tasks.summary: Implement the per-repository sighting file at ~/.insrc/team/seen/<16 hex sha256 of realpath>.json: read with shape validation (damaged is distinguishable from absent), unique-temp-name overwrite writer for refresh, create-only hard-link publish for the reader, removal, the anchor merge rule (a known anchor is never replaced by an unknown one), and the exclusive lock with the 30 second stale rule.
acceptanceChecks: Two repositories, including a symlinked path, get distinct keys from the real path.
A damaged sighting reads as damaged evidence, never as absent.
Create-only publish never overwrites an existing or damaged sighting; the overwrite writer uses a unique temp name.
The lock refuses a second holder, and takes over a lock older than 30 seconds.

tasks.title: AnchorFinder
tasks.summary: Implement the grandfathering anchor: the oldest add of .insrc/policy.json on the first-parent history of the tracking ref, with committer time in ISO form, known false and empty values for a shallow repository, a failed walk or no add found; a later delete and re-add never moves it.
acceptanceChecks: On a history with adoption, deletion and reintroduction the anchor is the adoption commit.
A depth-1 shallow clone gives known false with empty commit and time.
A failing git log gives known false without throwing.

tasks.title: PolicyReader
tasks.summary: Implement the synchronous, network-free reader in the HLD envelope: sighting checked first and taking precedence over every solo shortcut; branch from the sighting, else the remote HEAD, else unknown (remote is origin, else the sole remote, a sighting's recorded remote stays authoritative); read the policy from the tracking ref or the recorded commit; refuse with the team refresh --branch instruction only when a fetched tracking ref (symbolic HEAD skipped) carries the policy file while the branch is unknown; none when no sighting and no evidence; create-only sighting write on first observation; fill the derived source block including the anchor.
acceptanceChecks: The policy is read from the default branch tracking ref and working-tree or feature-branch edits have no effect.
Non-git, no-commit and no-remote directories without a sighting read as none with no write.
A known team repo whose remote was removed is refused or read from the recorded commit, never none.
An unknown default branch with a policy on a fetched ref is refused with the --branch instruction and no policy is applied; with no policy on any fetched ref it reads as none.
A never-fetched repo with no sighting reads as none.
The remote is origin when present, else the sole remote; several remotes without origin are not guessed (none without a sighting); a sighting's recorded remote stays authoritative.
The first observation creates the sighting create-only and a failed write never changes the result.

tasks.title: Default-branch resolution and pin verification
tasks.summary: Implement the refresh's branch decision: parse git ls-remote --symref output (the remote's answer wins over any pin), fall back to the branch recorded in a valid sighting, then to a supplied --branch name verified with git ls-remote --heads (non-empty output) and recorded with source user, otherwise refuse with the instruction to re-run with --branch; an unreachable remote or a missing branch records nothing.
acceptanceChecks: The remote's named default branch is used and overrides an earlier user pin; the supplied name is ignored.
With a dangling remote HEAD and no pin the result is a refusal asking for --branch.
A supplied branch is accepted only when ls-remote --heads prints it; a missing branch or an unreachable remote returns a reason and records nothing.

tasks.title: PolicyRefresh fetch and record
tasks.summary: Implement the guarded refresh sequence under the per-repository lock and one 10 second deadline: use the resolved branch, fetch only that branch with an explicit refspec, --refmap= and the isolating flags, read the policy from the updated tracking ref, find the anchor, write the sighting (or remove it when the file is absent) before the cosmetic remote HEAD update, return ok false when the sighting cannot be recorded after the ref moved, and treat a failed cosmetic update as a warning.
acceptanceChecks: Only the default branch tracking ref changes; no tag, other tracking ref, FETCH_HEAD or prune effect.
A refresh brings a changed policy into the tracking ref and the reader then applies it.
An unreachable remote reports failure and leaves the last fetched policy in use.

A sighting write failure reports failure, a cosmetic HEAD failure is only a warning (except where the HEAD still points at another retained branch, see the removal check), and a second refresh is refused while the lock is held.

The policy file removed from the default branch removes the sighting and the repo reads as none; the one exception is a remote HEAD that still points at another retained branch and cannot be updated, where the previous record is put back and the refresh fails closed so the old branch's policy cannot be resurrected.

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: Policy file parsing against the authored-fields schema: valid file, unknown field, wrong type, bad JSON, a file carrying claimUnits, forceTaskIssues or source
Sighting read and validation, branchSource remote or user, damaged sighting treated as evidence
Reader precedence: a sighting is checked before any solo shortcut; branch precedence is sighting branch, then remote HEAD, then unknown

Reader with an unknown default branch: refuses with the --branch instruction when a tracking ref carries the policy file, skips the symbolic HEAD, returns none when none does, and never applies a policy from an unlabelled ref
Reader create-only sighting write on first observation, never overwriting an existing or damaged sighting, failure not changing the result
Anchor parsing of git log output: the oldest add is chosen even after a later delete and re-add; shallow gives known false; a known anchor is never replaced by an unknown one
Refresh branch resolution: the remote's answer wins over a supplied branch, then the sighting's branch, then the supplied branch after verification
Sighting key derivation from the real path
StarterPolicyWriter no-clobber hard link
Reader returns the policy from the default branch's tracking ref and ignores working-tree and feature-branch edits
Reader returns ok none for a non-git directory, a repo with no commits and a repo with no remote when no sighting exists
Reader in a repo with a remote, the remote HEAD removed with git remote set-head -d and a fetched policy: refused with the --branch instruction; the same repo with no policy on any fetched ref: none
Regression: a known team repo whose remote was removed, whose clone has no commits or refs, or that is no longer a git repo is refused or read from the recorded commit, never read as none
Refresh isolation: only the default branch's tracking ref changes, with no tag, other branch, FETCH_HEAD or prune effect

Refresh with the remote HEAD dangling: refused without --branch; with --branch naming a real branch it records source user and fetches; with a missing branch name or an unreachable remote nothing is recorded
Refresh where the remote names its default branch overrides an earlier user pin
Refresh offline: unreachable remote leaves the last fetched policy in use, and a known team repo with nothing fetched is refused with the reason
Refresh step failures: sighting write failure reports failure, cosmetic HEAD failure is a warning only
Refresh lock: a second refresh is refused, a lock older than 30 seconds is taken over
Default-branch rename and policy file removal

Anchor on real history: adoption, approval, deletion, reintroduction keeps the adoption commit; a depth-1 shallow clone gives known false; deepening the history lets the next refresh record a known anchor
team init and team refresh dispatch, help lines and result lines, with an optional path and the context repo as default
team refresh --branch passes the name through to the service and renders the refusal that asks for it
A thrown error from either command rendered as a cross-prefixed line
The two Services test facades gain the team entry so the command tests run; no claim is made that they compile
